reason: Several Core routes answer 202 as their final response (missions, report renders, run retry, executions, draft notes, continue-as-mission, browser lease commands). Since 6607313 the GUI followed every 202 as a receipt, so a replayed final 202 looked pending: the GUI polled for 120 s and showed "Your request is saved", or showed it at once against a direct Core. Core now marks every receipt-following answer with X-Nebula-Request-State (complete / pending / needs-reconciliation) through one replay-header helper used by the API worker and Host Settings; the GUI, terminal client and Settings bridge stop on anything but pending, and without the marker treat only Core's receipt, status and chat-acceptance envelopes as pending. Selection: the API worker suite (new marker tests for receipt, status, final 202 replay on GET and POST retry, spoofed saved marker, 409, chat acceptance and stream hand-off, plus the existing replay and viewer tests), Host Settings replay, pending, uncertain and paired-receipt tests, the two Settings bridge tests that exercise the complete (not pending) path, the terminal transport suite (new marker and chat-acceptance cases) and the two terminal shell tests that follow saved receipts. Frontend: client.test.ts (its three cases red on main since 6607313 now pass), client.durableRequests.test.ts (new final-202, older/direct Core and chat-acceptance cases), durableRequests.test.ts and executionDraftTransport.test.ts (draft-note 202s).
exclusions: Not selected: test_runtime_host_settings.py's process-level tests (test_saved_session_credential_serves_first_chat_in_an_actual_retained_kernel, test_session_secret_rpc_requires_the_exact_lease_and_current_provider_reference), which also fail locally on origin/main, and the rest of that file and the bridge file, which do not reach the changed replay paths. No Playwright: the catalogued real-Core areas touching missions and reports (mission-supervisor-core, butler-reports) are Butler/LAN journeys that main does not run reliably; instead the create-mission (direct and receipt-followed) and Export PDF journeys were run with Playwright against a scratch supervisor Core on a LAN origin serving this branch's production build, in desktop Chromium and emulated iPhone WebKit (see the PR). No native code changed. PostgreSQL parametrizations are collected but skip in CI because these files are not in the workflow's PostgreSQL list; they passed locally on PostgreSQL 16. The legacy nebula-chat client (#1042, unmerged) uses the same accepted_receipt and gains the marker when it lands. No live or staging Core mutation, database backup, or deployment.
